personality_one_liner: A calm, trustworthy university mobility product that makes shared travel feel clear, safe and effortless.
principles: The landing experience may be expressive; the signed-in product should prioritise clarity and speed.
Use motion to explain state changes, hierarchy or progress. Never animate merely because space is available.
Trust and route information should be easier to scan than decorative content.
Prefer one strong action per surface over several equally loud actions.
Light mode is the default. Dark mode is optional and must be equally complete.
Do not use decorative match percentages. Compatibility shown to users must come from backend matching logic.
Trip Mode must represent persisted trip state, not a local visual toggle.

rules: Use display weight sparingly for page titles and key route names.
Body copy should remain compact and conversational.
Avoid all-caps labels except very short status labels.

spacing.rule: Use generous whitespace without oversized cards. Keep information density comfortable, especially on mobile.

navigation.rule: Do not add another primary tab unless it is central to Discover → Match → Request → Confirm → Trip Chat → Travel → Rate. Time-pass stays a secondary shortcut, not a sixth primary destination.

rules: Use subtle press scale or opacity feedback for touch targets.
Use skeletons for initial loading and inline progress for mutations.
Prefer cross-fades and small translations over dramatic spring effects.

allowed: Transient overlays when readability remains high

screens.name: LandingAuth
screens.layout: Keep the university/airport hero and purposeful aircraft motion. Authentication should sit in a clean, high-contrast surface with one obvious primary path and a quieter alternative path.

screens.name: HomeFeed
screens.layout: Start with greeting/context, route search and a small filter row. Rank useful journeys first. Ride cards prioritise route, departure time, compatibility/trust and one request action. Map and heatmap are secondary utilities.

screens.name: Matches
screens.layout: Show backend-ranked compatibility with clear reasons, time overlap, verified identity and one next action. Do not invent frontend scores.

screens.name: Explore
screens.layout: Use Explore for upcoming trips and secondary travel utilities. Keep confirmed journeys easy to reach, and keep route demand, Student ID and Time-pass subordinate to the journey lifecycle.

screens.name: PoolCreation
screens.layout: Single-column form with route first, date/time next, then preferences and context. Use progressive disclosure for optional details. Keep the submit action visible and show mutation progress.

screens.name: Profile
screens.layout: Identity and trust first: university verification, academic context, rating/reliability and completed travel. Settings and secondary utilities should not compete with trust signals.

screens.name: TimePass
screens.layout: Keep Time-pass secondary and lightweight. Prefer short travel-knowledge, clue and word games such as Travel Trivia, Word Scramble, Airport Codes, Destination Detective and Travel Reveal. Avoid heavy artwork and reflex arcade mini-games. Trivia rounds should avoid recently served questions and draw from a broad, stable bank. All games must support both themes.

interaction_rules: Every async action must show a pending state and disable duplicate submission.
Use at least 44px touch targets for primary interactive controls.
Keep destructive actions visually separate from everyday actions.
Empty states must explain what the user can do next.
Do not hide critical safety or request status behind long-press interactions.
Use haptics lightly for selection, successful confirmation and important travel-state changes.
instructions_to_main_agent: Default to the semantic theme tokens in app/frontend/src/theme.ts rather than hard-coded colours.
Do not increase the number of primary navigation items beyond five without an explicit product decision.
Keep the signed-in application visually quieter than the landing page.
Preserve existing backend behaviour while refactoring UI surfaces.
Never display compatibility percentages that are not returned by active backend matching logic.
Do not represent Trip Mode as a local-only global switch.
